threads.summary: The war chest flashed its first returns in week 1: Herbert 318-and-3, Egbuka's 2-TD debut, Croskey-Merritt's 82-and-a-score — in a 9.9-point loss to the champs. Converting, but not cashing yet.
Three straight finals appearances (runner-up 2022 and 2023, champion 2024), and the fourth-trip campaign opened 1-0 with a businesslike 143.72 — Wilson and Nacua both healthy and producing.
Sacko called Skattebo 'overated and about to be a bust' on July 29; Karim answered 'Skatt about to go gang busters!' three minutes later. Bouz won its opener; the grading period runs all season.

Plot twist: the backfield paid its bill in week 1 — Hubbard went 89 total yards and a TD — and MHJTIME lost anyway, 151.48 to 142.62, to the week's top score. The tax thesis survives; the invoice just came from the schedule this time.

The standings referendum is officially open, and week 1's first accusation was already filed: Nate demanded Kevin's expulsion for 'Tanking week 1' over the empty QB slot. The pick-hoarders vs. win-now scoreboard starts now.

The all-in year opened with the week's biggest margin (+34.94) and Lamar's 3-TD night — against the league's most broken roster. Brent declared Kelce's farewell ends with a ship, 'It's been decided.' The clock is still the story.

essay:
One night in late August, Nate looked at Zach's roster — Derrick Henry, Kyren Williams, the whole Island of Misfit WR1s — and typed the most confident sentence of the offseason: "Good to know. Ill start you off 0-1." Here is what that sentence forgot: the team he was burying played for the title last December. Then Sunday happened, and Monday happened, and Henry happened — 18 carries, 169 yards and 2 touchdowns against the Bills — and the Sleeping Giants hung 151.48 on MHJTIME, the biggest number of the opening week, in its only game between two teams with real January plans.

Six teams won this weekend. The better question is whose story actually moved. The champs didn't need theirs to. Kittler on the Roof has played in three straight finals, and the title defense opened like an errand: 143.72, Garrett Wilson and Puka Nacua combining for 225 receiving yards, nobody breaking a sweat, banner unthreatened. Ben spent the week enjoying Dallas's real-life chaos and let the roster do the talking — which is what three-straight-finals rosters get to do.

The louder development came from two franchises finding out mid-game who they are this year. Chudders — three straight losing seasons, eleven draft picks in July, the league's designated bench-presser next to the trophy case — walked into the champion's building and lost by single digits while Justin Herbert carved the Chiefs for 318 and three and rookie Emeka Egbuka scored twice on debut. A rebuild doesn't announce itself with a trophy; it announces itself with a loss that scares better teams. That was one. And MHJTIME, ten-and-four a year ago and holding the best receiver room in the league, put up 142.62 — more than two of the six winners managed — and lost anyway, because the schedule pointed the Giants at Nate in the one week they were incandescent. He did everything right except pick his opponent.

The bottom of the league supplied the comedy. Kevin needed a rival's Sunday-morning courtesy heads-up that his starting QB slot was empty — a favor he will never hear the end of. Oscar watched Xavier Worthy's shoulder leave the season early, watched Brock Bowers limp to 103 yards, watched his bench outscore his plans, and typed the sentence of the week: "I'm unraveling week 1." It's the kind of message a group chat never deletes.

One week settles nothing — but it points. Henry pointed at one more contending year for a roster everyone eulogized. Herbert pointed at a window opening a season early. Lamar's three touchdowns pointed at a Monks team that now has to prove it against somebody healthy. The calls below are on the record for December, which is the only month that grades them. The season's opening argument is filed. Court is in session all fall.

rankings.blurb: We drafted the obituary in August — preseason #11, "your WRs peaked when Fortnite did," veterans on borrowed time — for a franchise that played for the title last December. That's the part everyone kept skipping. This roster won twelve games back in 2022, made the finals last season, and has spent three years being old the way Henry is old: theoretically. Week 1 was the theory failing in public. 151.48 — the biggest number anyone posted — in the only matchup between two teams with championship intentions, with Henry hammering the Bills for 169 yards and 2 touchdowns on 18 carries and saving a permit-requiring stiff-arm for Monday night, and Jalen Hurts sneaking in 2 rushing scores against Dallas. Best of all, the win landed on the exact guy who promised to start you 0-1 — by 8.86, with the whole chat watching. One honest note for December, though: this column thinks age eventually gets a vote and pencils you fourth at the wire. You spent August advertising league-winner RBs. The ad now has to run for thirteen more weeks.

Three straight trips to the final — runner-up in '22, runner-up in '23, champion at 11-3 in '24 — and the fourth campaign opened like an errand: 143.72 to 133.82, never really in doubt, nobody above 19 points and nobody needed above 19. Garrett Wilson went 7-for-95 with a touchdown against the Steelers, Puka caught 10 balls for 130 against the Texans, and the Jaguars defense quietly stacked 16 on the Panthers. This is the franchise the preseason column ranked sixth and called drywall-ceilinged, and the drywall keeps outliving everybody's marble. For December: second at the wire, hosting in the playoffs, one win from a fourth consecutive final — at which point the league should just rename the trophy. Somebody has to come take the belt. Nobody so much as reached for it in week one.

Honesty about the win first: Father Time put up the second-lowest losing score of the week, so beating them by 15.2 proves roughly what the Monks' 35-point party downstairs proves — very little. What holds this franchise third is everything that predates Sunday. A title in 2023. Ten-and-four last year. The deepest roster in the league, which produced 135.88 on a day the quarterbacks were bad enough that Nate spent Monday night composing eulogies for them in the chat — Drake Maye's 287-with-a-pick against the Raiders was the best line in the room, and Nick Bosa's 6-tackle, one-sack, fumble-recovery day carried the flag instead. That's the floor, and the floor won comfortably. The December call is about the ceiling: this column has you finishing first at the wire, quarterback room and all. If that's wrong, it won't be wrong quietly.

Two days before kickoff, this franchise flipped rookie Quinshon Judkins for Courtland Sutton — a win-now move from a team that made the playoffs at 9-5 last year and knows its window is open. Then the window did what it's built to do: Josh Allen preached a 38.76-point sermon — 394 passing yards, four total touchdowns against the Ravens — Sutton caught a touchdown on arrival, and the 144.06 covered for an owner who admitted he whiffed "on each of my start / sit decisions." The suspension jokes ("Rasheeing the 2025 Season") are jokes with a due date, and one player supplied more than a quarter of the points. The posture is right and the weapon is real. December call: fifth — a good team with a great quarterback, waiting on the rest of its lineup card to match its trades.

Back in 2023 this franchise was in the toilet bowl. Last season it went 10-4 and made the playoffs. Week 1 belongs to that same climb, filed under the most productive loss in the league: 142.62 — more than two of the six winners scored — against the one opponent that beat it. Myles Garrett wrecked the Bengals for 2 sacks, Jayden Daniels stacked 233 passing yards and 68 on the ground against the Giants, and Chuba Hubbard — from the backfield Zach called "trash" in August — went for 89 total yards and a touchdown against the Jaguars. Even the alleged weakness showed up. Your own summer thesis: "I just need avg rb play. Elite everywhere else." Week 1 delivered exactly that and charged you a loss for scheduling reasons. So here it is in writing for December: top three at the wire. The 0-1 is a costume. The grievance is legitimate. Go take it out on Father Time.

The all-in year — Lamar, Kelce's farewell tour, almost no picks left in the drawer — opened with the week's biggest margin, and the fine print matters: the +34.94 came against the one roster that showed up broken. Lamar was genuinely great (209 passing yards, 70 rushing, 3 total touchdowns against the Bills), and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 124 receiving yards says the retool is real. None of it yet says whether a 7-7 team became a contender. Brent has already written the ending — Kelce brings the Monks their first ship, "It's been decided" — and this column's December call is sixth, the middle, again, unless the next statement win comes with a pulse attached. The clock, not the margin, is still the story.

Your 2022 title gets a year further away every autumn — 11-3 in '23, 7-7 in '24 — and the opener fit the arc: the lowest winning score of the week (131.72), Mahomes conjuring 26.02 against the Chargers, McCaffrey grinding out 142 total yards on 31 touches without a touchdown. Respectable, mortgage-paying football. Seventh in December, says this column, and every win above that is the old guard stealing one. #THORTONTIME remains a better bit than a plan.

Forget the loss for a second — this is a multi-year rebuild whose window finally looks open, and week 1 was the first hard evidence. Three straight losing seasons (4-10, 3-11, 4-10). Eleven picks in July's draft. The chat pricing "Bill" like a meme stock all August. And then the young roster walked into the champion's building and lost by only 9.9 while outscoring two of the week's winners — Justin Herbert sliced the Chiefs for 318 yards and 3 touchdowns, Emeka Egbuka scored twice on debut against the Falcons, and Jacory Croskey-Merritt ripped 82 yards and a touchdown on ten carries. You still couldn't get past Kittler, which is what champions are for — but for the first time since the trophy case got dusty, the weights look liftable. December call: eighth, and the happiest eighth-place team in the league. Keep the picks. The montage just cut to the fight.

Somewhere between 2-12 in 2022, 2-12 in 2024, and Sunday morning's rival courtesy heads-up "that you don't have a qb in the starting spot," this franchise's problem stopped being talent. Bijan went full Swiss-army against the Buccaneers — 100 receiving yards and a score out of the backfield — Breece Hall ran for 107 against the Steelers, and the 132.92 lost by 11 to a Josh Allen sermon, not to the empty lineup slot. The talent says top half. The operations say 2-12, twice. Ninth in December — with real upside the moment somebody sets two alarms.

Quiet franchise, quiet loss, quiet 120.68 — Brock Purdy's 277 yards with two picks, Kyle Hamilton's honest safety work, wagyu receivers served medium-rare. This team went 9-5 back in 2022 and has been under .500 both years since, and the loudest take of the owner's entire summer was "Tet all day." Tenth in December. The spoiler role is open year-round.

The franchise literally named itself after its rookie class — seven July picks including Trevor Etienne, Woody Marks, and Luther Burden — then opened the season with a box score whose top three lines were a quarterback, a defense, and a kicker. Justin Jefferson deserves better company than a 120.32 loss to the week's lowest-scoring winner, and the commissioner spent the run-up workshopping your team name into a punchline. Stars-without-support was the preseason "Fraud" ruling; week 1 declined the appeal. Eleventh in December — and the rookies decide everything after that.

A year removed from 3-11, the retooling franchise with the famous pick stash needed exactly one afternoon to start unraveling: Worthy's shoulder gone almost immediately ("Xavier worthy season over," the chat ruled within minutes), Brock Bowers gutting out 103 receiving yards while visibly hurting, the bench outscoring the plan, and the owner posting "I'm unraveling week 1" before Monday even arrived. The 109.42 was the week's lowest score, taken in its biggest beatdown, and Cam Little's perfect 4-for-4 leg landing among your top three scorers was the tell. Deebo led the wideouts with 77 yards, five weeks after "Deebo about to be WR1." Twelfth in December — the picks don't suit up, and this year the plan might not either.

confessionals.text: I scored 142.62. More than two teams that WON. I lose. The team I publicly promised to start 0-1 scored 151 in the one week the schedule pointed them at me. My backfield was supposed to be the problem — Chuba scored a touchdown! I did everything right and the universe filed it under L. Fine. FINE. Daniel Jones is available, by the way. Danny Dimes is QB2 in all of fantasy football. I have receipts for everything.

Biggest margin of the week and the column wants to talk about 'opponent quality' like some kind of lawyer. Lamar had three touchdowns. Kelce is going to stand on business in his last year and bring the Monks their first ship — it's been decided, because I decided it. Sixth? Fine. Write it down. Frame it. I'll be collecting apologies in December, cash or Venmo.

Yes, the QB slot was empty on Sunday morning. Yes, Patrick sent a 'courtesy heads up.' Yes, Nate called for my expulsion. You know what nobody's talking about? Bijan caught six balls for a hundred yards. Breece went for 107. I lost by 11 to a Josh Allen sermon, not to my lineup screen. The roster is fine. The roster is FINE. I just need to set an alarm. Two alarms.

Worthy's shoulder. Bowers limping. My bench going off while my starters filed workers' comp. I posted 'I'm unraveling week 1' as a joke, and then the scoreboard made it a documentary. Brent hung 144 on me and had the nerve to be gracious about it. It's week one. It's WEEK ONE. I have picks. I have time. I do not currently have a functioning wide receiver room. But I have picks, and I have time.

mailbag.question: Dear Commish: I won by 34.94 points — the biggest margin of the week — and you have me SIXTH, behind a team that LOST. Explain yourself. — GauchoTrain
mailbag.answer: Gladly. You beat the only roster in the league that was actively falling apart, your 7-7 from last season didn't retire over the summer, and the 0-1 team above you outscored two of this week's winners against the best team in the league. Rankings weigh who you beat, not just by how much. Beat a live opponent and the top four is right there — the horses are real. Kelce hive, remain calm.

mailbag.question: @rango_ asks: I outscored two teams that won this week. A loss. Be honest with me — who do I sue?
mailbag.answer: The scheduling algorithm, and good luck: it has no assets and a great lawyer. You're the best 0-1 team this column has ever ranked fifth — and it just put a December top-three call on you in writing. Win the games where you're the better roster, which is most of them, and this becomes a funny story you tell at the draft.

mailbag.question: From the group chat: "just a courtesy heads up that you don't have a qb in the starting spot." Discuss.
mailbag.answer: The most polite act of psychological warfare in league history. Patrick gets a sportsmanship nod, Kevin gets a public-service reminder that rosters don't set themselves, and the rest of us get a banner quote for the ages. Set your lineups, people. It's week one, not week eleven.

mailbag.question: Dear Commish: You ranked General Ken-obi #1 in the preseason, he won by 15, and now he's third. What more do you want from the man?
mailbag.answer: A win over somebody breathing, mostly — Father Time put up the week's second-lowest losing score, so Sunday told us little we didn't already know. The résumé is why he's third and not lower: a 2023 title, 10-4 last year, the deepest roster in the league. And the December call on record here is still Ken-obi first at the wire. Third is a September address, not a verdict.

bits.title: Great Call of the Week
bits.text: Zach, back in August: "I've got league winner RBs." Derrick Henry, Monday night: 169 yards, 2 touchdowns, and a stiff-arm that should require a permit. Sometimes the ad copy is just true.

bits.title: Overheard in the Chat
bits.text: "Kick him out of the league.  Tanking week 1" — Nate, displaying his trademark restraint roughly ninety seconds after Patrick's courtesy heads-up about Kevin's empty QB slot.

bits.title: Preseason Prediction Tracker
bits.text: Karim, September 2023: "You soo high you think you got the second best team in the league rn." Two years on, Chudders opened with another loss — but held the champs to single digits and got 3 touchdowns from Herbert. Aging badly, but aging interestingly.

bits.title: Things I Believe But Can't Prove
bits.text: The Judkins-for-Sutton swap gets cited in a heated group chat argument by Thanksgiving. Sutton caught a touchdown for his new team on day one; Nate admitted it "Hurt to let go Sutton." Both sides convinced they won — that's how you know it was a real trade.

bits.title: Luck Index
bits.text: MHJTIME scored more than two of this week's six winners and lost. Ghastly scored less than everyone and lost by the most. One of these teams should feel unlucky. The other should feel seen.

picks.blurb: The prove-it game arrives immediately. Burden's quarterback-defense-kicker offense visits a Monks team that just dropped 144, and if Lamar repeats even 80% of Week 1, this ends early. The 'beat somebody with a pulse' clause gets its first test — a pulse is present here, if faint.

Kevin will absolutely set his lineup this week — public shame is the league's most reliable alarm clock — but a champ at operating temperature is a brutal draw for a team still running fire drills. Kittler just won comfortably without a single monster performance. That's the scary version.

The lowest winning score of Week 1 hosts the lowest score, period. Mahomes and McCaffrey against a wounded Grayskull roster missing Worthy should be merciful and brief. If Bouz can't clear 140 against this, the aging-core alarm gets audibly louder.

Yes, really. Herbert just carved the Chiefs for 318 and 3, Egbuka looks like an instant starter, and Rasheeing needed a 38.76-point Josh Allen miracle to paper over self-admitted lineup whiffs. If Allen is merely human for one Sunday, the rebuild collects its first scalp.

An angry, elite roster that just dropped 142 in a loss now draws the league's quietest offense. Nate is insufferable after wins; after an unlucky loss he's a public hazard. Father Time should request a wellness check before kickoff.

The marquee: preseason #1 hosting the team that just torched the preseason #3. Saquon against Henry, receipts against receipts. Blake's quarterbacks cannot possibly stay this quiet — but Zach's veterans just made the loudest statement of Week 1, and I ride hot hands in September. Give me the points and the right to regret it.

special_picks.stay_away: General Ken-obi vs Sleeping Giants — I picked it, and I already regret it
special_picks.teaser: Kittler on the Roof -7.0 with MHJTIME -9.5: the two angriest good teams in the league, teased together
